activity_context.topic_title: Calculating Volumes of Solids Using Triple Integrals

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Volume of a Solid Given a Diagram
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064036/assets/043adf0ef683c24fbf4680145411d86fa94b52016bee44ac8f08ca7c5ca9f1b7.png)

 

Find the volume of the solid region above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the top one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
examples.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064036/assets/75a76a2dbc34c889335e66623e12b686eb9a255ee0d67f9be0e3792f2650360c.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type I region

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (x,y) \in D, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 4-x-y \big\},
$$

where

$$
D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 2 \big\}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064036/assets/e19ffe6a0555851c2b05526272beb21dbcdc082a23a2e11809c661666efdf133.png)

Hence, the type I representation of $R$ is

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 4-x-y \big\}.
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{4-x-y}dz\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}[z]_{z=0}^{z=4-x-y}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}(4-x-y)-0\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}4-x-y\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[(4-x)y-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}((4-x)(2)-\frac{{2}^{2}}{2})-0\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}6-2x\,dx \\  & =[6x-{x}^{2}]_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =(6(1)-{1}^{2})-0 \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the volume of the solid $R,$ given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,1\le z\le 3,\,0\le x\le 2z\operatorname{sin}⁡y}.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that we have a three-dimensional type II region.

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2z\operatorname{sin}⁡y}\,dx\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{1}^{3}[x]_{x=0}^{x=2z\operatorname{sin}⁡y}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{1}^{3}2z\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,{[{z}^{2}]}_{z=1}^{z=3}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y({3}^{2}-{1}^{2})\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}8\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dy \\  & =8[-\operatorname{cos}⁡y]_{y=0}^{y=\pi /2} \\  & =-8(0-1) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
